title: Cylindrical Geodesic Flow Matching for Quasiperiodic Physiological Signal Transformation
description: NeurIPS 2026 Main Conference, Sydney. This work introduces a flow matching method for paired cardiovascular waveform translation that replaces the standard affine path with a closed-form geodesic on the phase-amplitude cylinder, outperforming interpolation baselines on zero-shot photoplethysmography and limited-support seismocardiography adaptation benchmarks.

title: Towards Monitoring Acute Opioid Withdrawal Severity Using a Multimodal Wearable Chest Patch
description: ACM Transactions on Computing for Healthcare. This study characterizes 32 cardiorespiratory features from wearable signals in 16 individuals with opioid use disorder over 7 days, identifying features that differ between high and low withdrawal and classifying withdrawal severity with machine learning.

title: EffSCG: Real-Time Seismocardiogram Denoising on Edge Devices
description: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics. This work presents an optimization framework that lets a deep learning seismocardiogram denoiser run directly on resource-constrained wearables, cutting inference time and memory footprint without substantive accuracy loss.

title: SCRIBE: Simultaneous Cardiac and Respiratory Impedance Biomarkers with Electromechanics
description: IEEE Sensors Journal. This work presents SCRIBE, a compact, flexible chest patch that concurrently measures cardiac and respiratory mechanics using ECG, seismocardiography, photoplethysmography, and bioimpedance.

title: Seismocardiography Pig Hypovolemia Dataset for Signal Quality Indexing and Validated Cardiac Timings
description: Scientific Data. This study introduces a validated dataset of porcine seismocardiogram heartbeats, expertly annotated for cardiac timings and signal quality to benchmark non-invasive monitoring. These high-quality labels address a critical data scarcity, enabling the training of supervised deep learning models to automate signal denoising, feature extraction, and fiducial point detection.

title: IEEE Body Sensor Networks Presentation in Los Angeles
description: Presented research on the quantification of opioid withdrawal through seismocardiogram variability from wearable CardioTag devices.

title: Characterizing Central-Autonomic Dynamics during an Episodic Memory Task
description: IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering. This study analyzes coupling between the central and autonomic nervous systems in 67 healthy adults during an episodic memory task, using EEG alongside ECG and seismocardiogram signals.

title: Quantifying Opioid Withdrawal through Cardio-mechanical Variability using Multimodal Wearable Sensors
description: IEEE BSN conference. This study demonstrates a significant correlation between cardio-mechanical variability (SCG signals) and subjective withdrawal severity, proposing a new objective biomarker for monitoring recovery.
